title: GovernanceBench: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating AI Governance Document Understanding

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a benchmark accelerates compliance tool development, but the path from benchmark existence to actual safety improvement requires others to build on it.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: constructing QA pairs from governance documents and running LLM evaluations is doable for CS students with guidance, though requires careful question design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: covering multiple governance documents, generating quality QA pairs, and evaluating multiple LLMs requires steady work but has clear milestones.

evidence: AI Act Evaluation Benchmark (arXiv:2603.09435, March 2026) provides exactly this: an open, transparent, reproducible evaluation dataset for NLP and RAG systems on EU AI Act governance documents, including risk-level classification, article extraction, obligation generation, and QA tasks
NLP for Local Governance Meeting Records (arXiv:2602.08162, 2026) reviews NLP tasks for governance document understanding
Government Affairs Domain benchmark (ACM TIST 2025) evaluates LLMs on official document processing and government QA

elimination_reason: Already solved: AI Act Evaluation Benchmark (arXiv:2603.09435, March 2026) provides an open benchmark dataset for NLP and RAG evaluation on AI governance documents with QA, classification, and extraction tasks -- directly duplicating the proposed project.
